summary: Texas beat Ole Miss 34-27. ESPN reports Goosby is out for the season, while Mississippi State is still evaluating Taylor. Protection and quarterback preparation lead the next week.

items.headline: ESPN reports Goosby will miss the rest of the season
items.tldr: Cojoe replaced Goosby against Ole Miss. Watch the left tackle’s pass sets and the help Texas gives him before asking the passing game to hold the ball.

items.headline: Mississippi State is still evaluating Taylor’s injury
items.tldr: Lebby said Monday that the staff needs more time to evaluate Taylor. Prepare for both quarterbacks; the next availability report should guide the matchup plan.

items.headline: Texas beats Ole Miss, 34-27
items.tldr: Brown ran for 157 yards. Carry that ground-game production forward while cleaning up possessions that let a game get tight again.

items.headline: Biles earns SEC co-defensive player of the week
items.tldr: Biles intercepted a pass on fourth-and-goal against Ole Miss. Watch how linebacker pressure and coverage work together when the offense reaches the red zone.

items.headline: Mississippi State visits Texas at 6:30 p.m. CT Saturday
items.tldr: The October 31 kickoff is set. Plan for another evening in Austin; use the schedule panel for the updated broadcast assignment.

lead.headline: Protect the next possession.
lead.body: Start with the blind side. Build quick passing answers and a dependable run game before asking the quarterback to rescue a broken down. On defense, make the pocket close without surrendering the escape lane.

matchup.thesis: Win the down before extending the play
matchup.question: How should Texas approach Mississippi State?
matchup.answer: Make protection and the first read work together. Take the available gain, keep the quarterback out of avoidable contact and force the opponent to sustain a drive against disciplined pursuit.

signals.title: Blind-side protection
signals.summary: Give the tackle a usable answer
signals.detail: Watch the first pass set, the chip help and the quarterback’s release. Judge the protection plan by whether it creates a clean decision.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with blind-side protection?

signals.title: Quarterback preparation
signals.summary: Build both versions of the plan
signals.detail: Keep quarterback availability separate from assumptions about mobility. Set the edge, close the escape lane and make the throw come from a controlled pocket.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with quarterback preparation?

signals.title: Early downs and ground-game continuity
signals.detail: Watch the block at the point of attack and the runner’s decision through the crease. A reliable early-down gain should leave the passing game an easier job.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with early downs and ground-game continuity?

signals.title: Pressure and coverage
signals.detail: Pair the pass rush with coverage that survives the quarterback’s first escape. Finish the tackle and defend the goal line without giving away a free completion.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with pressure and coverage?
